findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the cold brew dispenser, creamer dispenser, and tea machine to be soiled. The PIC was informed and plans to have staff clean the equipment. The PIC stated that the machines are cleaned routinely and staff have an assigned machine that they are responsible for maintaining. Ensure staff monitor the equipment and clean them as often as necessary to prevent an accumulation of soil.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues [C].

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the flooring under the soda syrup boxes to be soiled with spilled syrup. The PIC was informed and plans to clean the floors. Ensure the floors are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing [C].

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed sanitizer bucket near soda fountains at 100 ppm. This is below the required range of 200-400 ppm. CORRECTED- PIC changed the bucket. Use facility test strips to regularly monitor sanitizer concentration and change buckets during continuous use.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. (P)

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed staff-prepared quaternary sanitizer bottle in back of house to be at 800 ppm. The law requires 200-400 ppm for proper sanitizing of food contact surfaces. CORRECTED Inspector diluted water to bottle to bring it to 400 ppm. Inspector discussed observations and actions taken with PIC. [P]
findings.citation_text: 7-202.12(A) Conditions of Use. POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS shall be: (A) Used according to: (1) LAW and this Code, (2) Manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions that state that use is allowed in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, (3) The conditions of certification, if certification is required, for use of the pest control materials, and (4) Additional conditions that may be established by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspector observed cutting boards and utensils stored behind triple sink. Discussed with PIC need for food contact surfaces to be in a located in an area away from splash and possible cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed mold at south wall near soda syrup racks. Repair the wall to eliminate mold, and address the source of the moisture to prevent future accumulation. Walls, floors, and drains shall be maintained in good repair. 

In addition, a portion of the wall behind the soda fountain station has been removed to access floor drain for cleaning and maintenance. This addressed complaint that originated this visit. This has been an ongoing issue, which has initiated previous visits by SCDPH. PIC stated that maintenance serviced drain lines this afternoon and there is a remodel planned in the future.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.12(B) Floors, Walls, and Ceilings, Utility Lines. (B) Exposed utility service lines and pipes shall be installed so they do not obstruct or prevent cleaning of the floors, walls, or ceilings. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Numerous drain flies are present around the customer side and back access to the soda fountain. Clean the area and continue pest control to eliminate drain flies. 
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Numerous drain flies are present around the customer side and back access to the soda fountain. Clean the area and continue pest control to eliminate drain flies. 
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
There is a moisture problem under the soda fountain resulting in mold growth on the walls and surfaces in the area. Fix the problem to eliminate the moisture.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The area under the soda fountain is littered with trash accumulation and walls are moldy. The area is only accessible  through the small hole cut in the back wall. Clean this area frequently enough to prevent accumulation of trash and mold growth.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Spills/soil accumulation observed 1) below the milk rack in the walk-in cooler; and 2) under the soda syrups rack near the walk-in freezer. Clean floors.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-bucket at food service area was observed below 100ppm. Store manager noted food service employee was in the process of changing solutions. After changing solutions one sani-bucket still registered concentration below 200ppm. Time stamp on bucket was 9:44am, but food service employee stated it was changed at the same time as other solutions. Solution in question was remade and observed at 200-400ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Manager in charge at the time of inspection has not yet completed a food manager course. Manager stated the company is in the process of getting him registered. Another person with a food manager certification was on-site but was not the designated person in charge (PIC). Ensure all managers that have the potential to be the designated PIC at time of inspection has a food manager certification.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-bucket had a concentration below 100ppm. Required concentration per product use directions is 200-400ppm. Fresh solution was provided at 200ppm. Ensure sanitizer solutions are changed throughout the day and maintained at proper concentration.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee did not wash hands between tasks and was observed working the cash register prior to going to food service area. Employee was observed opening the lid to the roller grill and checking products. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed, and staff were observed washing hands between tasks for the remainder of inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11 Hand soap was not available at the handsink in the food service area. A small bottle of soap was provided. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the handsinks at the food service area or in the back by the walkin cooler. Handwashing signage was provided during inspection. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handsink at the food service counter has been used as a dump sink based on information provided. Proper use of handsink was discussed.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using the food service counter handsink as a dump sink for coffee.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Ice shoots of the soda machines were observed with pink mold accumulation on lower/back edges. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment such as beverage dispensing equipment shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. 
Food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Chili sauce dispensed from the Gehl's dispenser had an internal temperature 127F-130F. Cheese sauce dispensed from the other side of the same dispenser had an internal temperature of 135F-140F. Thermometer on the side of the dispenser was reading around 130F. Upon further investigation store manager discovered the valve for the chili sauce was not properly attached to the bag, which was allowing air into the product. Chili sauce was removed for discard. Ensure that products are properly hooked up in the dispenser to allow for consistent hot holding at 135F/above throughout the product. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Open creamers in dispensers had date marks of 10/3-10/10. With product being opened on 10/3 the discard date was 10/9. All creamers were discarded and replaced with fresh product.
Open packages of hotdogs in the walkin cooler had date marks of 10/7 with a discard date indicated as 10/17. Store manager changed the date to reflect proper discarded date of 10/13. 
Ready to eat TCS foods shall be clearly dated after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Packages of bottled water available for purchase were observed outside the facility on display. Manager was advised the bottled water needs to be stored in the facility. Cease the practice of displaying bottled water outside the facility. 
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Wiping cloth was observed with a spray bottle of sanitizer. Manager was advised on use of disposable paper towels when spray bottle of sanitizer is in use. Otherwise, damp wiping cloths need to be stored in a sanitizer solution between uses. Wiping cloth was moved to soiled linen storage. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Whipped topping at coffee counter was not date marked. Once placed in the dispenser, the product is good at ambient temperature for 5 days. Manager noted the product was opened 2 days prior. Benefit of doubt was given; product was dated and kept for use.

All foods that require date marks need to be properly dated and used or discarded w/in the time frame allowed for use. Make sure the whipped topping is dated when opened and placed in the dispenser and used or discarded w/in 5 days. 
Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food (e.g. hotdogs) shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.140(a) - Built in digital thermometer in the back of the sandwich cooler was not functioning. Get the built in thermometer repaired and/or provide another properly functioning hanging thermometer in the cooler.

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee went between tasks and did not wash hands. Employee was working at the front register and then stocked cups at the soda fountain. Washing hands between tasks and before handling food, clean equipment, and single service articles was discussed with manager.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Educational handouts on handwashing and glove use were provided.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Employee drinks were observed on shelving over the 3 part sink, in the pizza freezer, and in the pizza prep area. All drinks were moved or discarded during inspection.
Proper storage of personal beverages was discussed.

A food employee make drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee's hands, the container, and exposed food; clean equipment; utensils and linens, and unwrapped single service articles. Provide cups with a lid and straw and store them in an area that does not pose a potential risk of cross contamination.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
(R) 750.830g - Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer concentration. Obtain and use a quat test kit
for checking sanitizer concentrations in spray bottles and 3 part sink during ware washing. 

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) oven in prep area - 1. bottom inside (carbon buildup), 2. edge beneath the door (carbon/food debris), & 3. counter under the oven (dust);
B) counter under equipment at food counter (dust/food crumbs);  and
C) inside cabinet under soda machine (splash/moisture).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Boxes of single service items (cups, creamers) were observed on the floor in the storage room, by the pizza freezer, in the hallway by the restrooms, and in the store across from reach-in cooler section. Some items were delivered two days prior. Manager noted she is in the process of re-organizing the storage area. Manager was advised all single service cups, creamers, food and food related items must be stored at least 6 inches off the floor regardless of packaging and current state of re-organization. 

Sleeves of cups were observed in the cabinet beneath the soda machine. The drain was soiled with heavy buildup and condensation was present in the cabinet as well as on the packaging of the cups. Cups were removed from the cabinet.

Single service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text:
750.1170 - West front door was not properly closing flush with the door frame. Gaps were present at the top and bottom on the left side of the door. Manager placed a work order; ticket number was provided during phone conversation (see general comments).

Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - Trim along bottom right side of mopsink along the floor to wall juncture was damaged. Debris accumulation was observed in the resulting crevice. Clean the area and provide proper repairs.

Drain under soda machine was soiled with heavy mold accumulation. Clean the drain.

Drain by the back door for walkin cooler condensate line was soiled with buildup in the bottom. Clean all the floor drains throughout as needed to eliminate buildup.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1210 - Ceiling in walkin cooler was soiled with dust around the fans and what appeared to be drink splash near the reach-in cooler doors. Fan covers were also soiled with dust accumulation. Clean the ceiling in the walkin cooler and the fan covers as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Restroom exhaust vent covers were starting to acccumulate dust. Clean the vent covers in the restrooms.

Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - Bottle of Frebreeze spray was observed on the back ledge of the oven in prep area. Air freshener was removed from the prep area.
Employee purse was observed on top of the pizza freezer in an area used for food prep. Purse was moved to a storage locker.

An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text:
750.1390 - Wet mop heads were stored on the floor next to the mopsink and in the mopsink basin. The mopsink is right next to the clean dish drain board of the 3 part sink and staff need to be mindful of proper storage to minimize potential for cross contamination as well as potential water sources for drain flies. Store mops in a manner that allows for proper drying of wet mop heads.

Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored properly.
